"**Chihiro** " is a song by the American singer-songwriter [Billie Eilish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Eilish "Billie Eilish"). The third track on her third studio album, _[Hit Me Hard and Soft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft "Hit Me Hard and Soft")_ (2024), it was released to Italian [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") stations on January 17, 2025, via [EMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Records "EMI Records"). The song was written by Eilish and her brother [Finneas O'Connell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finneas_O'Connell "Finneas O'Connell"), who also produced the track for Darkroom and [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records").
## Background and release
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chihiro_\(song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")]
[![A man and a woman sitting on stage, both holding guitars with microphones.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/BillieEilishO2160622_%2843_of_45%29_%2852152970696%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-BillieEilishO2160622_%2843_of_45%29_%2852152970696%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BillieEilishO2160622_\(43_of_45\)_\(52152970696\)_\(cropped\).jpg)[Billie Eilish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Eilish "Billie Eilish") (_right_) and her brother [Finneas O'Connell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finneas_O'Connell "Finneas O'Connell") (_left_) performing in June 2022
On April 12, 2024, in an interview with [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music")'s presenter [Zane Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zane_Lowe "Zane Lowe"), Eilish teased a 15-second [snippet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampling_\(music\) "Sampling \(music\)") of "Chihiro", which was released on her third studio album, _[Hit Me Hard and Soft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft "Hit Me Hard and Soft")_ (2024).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-:1-1) The song's title is a reference to Chihiro Ogino, the main character of the 2001 [Studio Ghibli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Ghibli "Studio Ghibli") animated film _[Spirited Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away "Spirited Away")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-:2-2) In an interview with Angie Martoccio of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ , Eilish said:[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-:0-3)
> The song is loosely based off of that movie, which is one of my favorites. It’s kind of from her point of view, mixed with mine. The visuals in that movie are some of the best ever—all that Studio Ghibli shit is unbelievable ... There’s all those visuals of the train in the water after the flood, and it literally looks like an ocean with a train track. I had just watched _Spirited Away_ and [brother-and-frequent-collaborator] [Finneas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finneas "Finneas") had made that beat. I love that movie. I’ve seen it so many times.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-:0-3)
"Chihiro" was written by Eilish and Finneas; the latter also produced the song.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-4) It was recorded in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), California, United States.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-5)
"Chihiro" was previewed with "[Lunch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunch_\(song\) "Lunch \(song\)")" and "[L'Amour de Ma Vie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Amour_de_Ma_Vie "L'Amour de Ma Vie")" at [Coachella 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_2024 "Coachella 2024").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-:3-6) On May 10, 2024, Eilish released a 49-second-long clip of "Chihiro" through the [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel of the rhythm game _[Fortnite Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite_Festival "Fortnite Festival")_ because it was confirmed the song would be included as a [backing track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backing_track "Backing track") on the third season of the game.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-7) "Chihiro" is the third song on _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ ;[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-8) it was released with the studio album on May 17, 2024,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-9) through Darkroom and [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-Observer-10)
Eilish and Finneas hosted free listening parties prior to the album's release; [American Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Express "American Express") presented a party on May 15 at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in Brooklyn, New York, and another on May 16 at the [Kia Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kia_Forum "Kia Forum") in [Inglewood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood,_California "Inglewood, California"), in association with [Snapchat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapchat "Snapchat").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-11) On May 15 at the Barclays Center, "Chihiro" garnered some of the evening's most-enthusiastic crowd response.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-12)
"Chihiro" was released as a single in Italy on January 16, 2025, through [EMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Records "EMI Records").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-13)
## Composition and lyrics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chihiro_\(song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition and lyrics")]
"Chihiro" is a [mid-tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-tempo "Mid-tempo")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-Guardian-14) [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-15) [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-16) and [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") song[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-Observer-10) that incorporates elements of [progressive R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_soul "Progressive soul")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-17) and [tech house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tech_house "Tech house").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-18) In the lyrics, Eilish sings of feelings of being lost and found that are reminiscent of the _Spirited Away_ character Ogino Chihiro.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-:0-3)
## Commercial performance
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chihiro_\(song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Commercial performance")]
After the release of _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ on May 17, 2024, "Chihiro" made its debut at number six on the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-19) It debuted at number 12 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-20) and at number three on the [US Hot Rock & Alternative Songs chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Rock_&_Alternative_Songs "Hot Rock & Alternative Songs").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-21) Additionally, the song debuted at number seven on the [UK Top 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Top_10 "UK Top 10").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-22)
A remix named as "MTG Chihiro" by [Mulú](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mul%C3%BA "Mulú") was initially denied permission for releasing on streaming platforms by Billie Eilish's management, including her brother Finneas.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-24) After negotiations, Eilish's team allowed [Duda Beat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duda_Beat "Duda Beat") to record the remixed version.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-25) It combines the track with [Brazilian funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_funk "Brazilian funk") elements and gained significant popularity on social media platforms, particularly [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-26) where it became the soundtrack for the "passinho Chihiro" dance.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-27)

## Music video
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chihiro_\(song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music video")]
The music video for "Chihiro" was teased on June 5, 2024, when Eilish shared on social media a short video in which she runs down a hallway. It premiered on Eilish's [Vevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vevo "Vevo") channel on YouTube at 09:00 [Pacific Daylight Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Daylight_Time "Pacific Daylight Time") (PDT) on June 6.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-MV-31) Eilish directed the music video and stars in it alongside [Nat Wolff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nat_Wolff "Nat Wolff").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\)#cite_note-MVNatt-32)
